answer: Delegation-depth decay keeps a Sybil swarm small: influence passed from one identity to the next loses a fixed share at every hop, like a garden where each cutting grows weaker than its parent. A single operator's thousand fakes all trace back to one root, so their combined weight stays near the root's own — the sparrow cannot lift a mountain by cloning itself. Each delegation is a pearl on a string, and the string only reaches so far; buying real weight means buying real, independent roots, which costs as much as being honest.
